title: Massive haemothorax
stem: Resus 1. A 34-year-old motorcyclist hit a lamp post at speed and struck the right side of his chest on the handlebars. The ambulance is two minutes out: HR 128, BP 84/52, RR 30, SpO2 90% on a non-rebreather, GCS 14. You lead the trauma team. The nurse, the paramedic and the examiner are in the bay.

review.text: Initial fluid. Your notes on haemorrhagic shock start with a 1–2 L saline bolus. ATLS now limits crystalloid to 1 L at most and moves early to blood (1:1:1), with permissive hypotension until the bleeding is controlled (not in head injury). 2 L of saline is scored as a trap.

notes:
Checked against ATLS 11th edition (2025; xABCDE, early blood), RCEM/NICE NG39 major trauma, CRASH-2 (tranexamic acid) and BTS/ATLS chest drain practice.

Massive haemothorax: more than 1500 mL of blood on insertion of the drain, or more than one third of the patient's blood volume. Thoracotomy is indicated for 1500 mL immediately, 200 mL/h for 2 to 4 hours, or a continuing need for transfusion. The decision rests on the patient's physiology as much as the volume.

ATLS 10th recommended a 28 to 32 Fr drain for haemothorax. Smaller drains (14 Fr pigtail) work for stable, non-massive haemothorax in trials (Kulvatunyou 2021), but a large-bore drain remains standard for a massive, clotting bleed. The station scores a large-bore drain.

Fluids: ATLS now limits crystalloid (at most 1 L) and moves to blood early in a 1:1:1 ratio; permissive hypotension (systolic around 80 to 90) until bleeding is controlled, unless there is a brain injury. Your notes on haemorrhagic shock say a 1 to 2 L saline bolus first; current practice is blood first, so 2 L of saline is scored as a trap.

Tranexamic acid 1 g over 10 minutes, then 1 g over 8 hours, only within 3 hours of injury (CRASH-2).

Safe triangle: anterior border of latissimus dorsi, lateral border of pectoralis major, a line level with the nipple (5th intercostal space), apex below the axilla. Go over the top of the rib to avoid the neurovascular bundle. Never use the trocar.

steps.label: Get the bay ready
steps.hint: Before he arrives: trauma call, PPE, blood to the bedside, rapid infuser and warmer, chest drain kit.

opts.t: Put out a trauma team call
opts.mark: Activates the trauma team before arrival
opts.r: Nurse Lam: Trauma call is out.

opts.t: Everyone in gloves, apron, eye protection
opts.mark: Team in PPE

opts.t: O-negative blood to the bedside; activate the massive haemorrhage protocol
opts.mark: Blood ready and massive haemorrhage protocol activated early

opts.t: Rapid infuser with a warmer, warm blankets
opts.mark: Prevents hypothermia: warmed products, blankets

opts.t: Open a chest drain tray and ultrasound at the bedside
opts.mark: Anticipates the chest: drain tray and ultrasound ready

opts.t: Book a CT scanner slot straight from the ambulance bay
opts.r: He is shocked. CT is for patients who respond; he goes to resus first.

opts.t: Hang 2 L of 0.9% saline on a pressure bag
opts.r: Large crystalloid volumes dilute clotting factors and worsen acidosis. Blood first.

steps.label: Paramedic handover
steps.hint: Take a structured handover: age, time, mechanism, injuries, signs, treatment.

Mechanism.r: Motorcycle into a lamp post at about 60 km/h, 35 minutes ago. Right chest onto the handlebars.
Mechanism.mark: Asks the mechanism and time of injury

Mechanism.r: Full-face helmet, thrown about 3 metres. Never unconscious according to bystanders.

Injuries.r: Bruised right chest wall, painful right side. Abrasions to both forearms. Nothing else obvious.

Signs.t: Vital signs and how they have changed?
Signs.r: First set: HR 110, BP 102/64. Now HR 128, BP 84/52. Getting worse.
Signs.mark: Asks the trend of the vital signs

Treatment.r: Oxygen 15 L. One 18 G in the left arm. 250 mL saline. Morphine not given yet.

steps.label: Primary survey
steps.hint: xABCDE: look, feel, percuss and listen to the chest; check circulation and pelvis without springing it.

x A.mark: Checks for exsanguinating external haemorrhage first

x A.r: He answers in short sentences. Airway patent. Collar and blocks on; manual in-line stabilisation while you look.
x A.mark: Airway patent; maintains spinal motion restriction

Breathing.r: Handlebar bruise over the right lower chest. Right side moves less. RR 30.
Trachea central. Tender right 5th to 7th ribs, no crepitus, no surgical emphysema.
Stony dull at the right base and mid zone. Resonant on the left.
Breathing.mark: Finds dullness to percussion on the right

Breathing.r: Breath sounds much reduced on the right. Normal on the left.
Breathing.mark: Finds reduced breath sounds on the right

Circulation.r: Thready radial pulse 128. Cold, pale, clammy. Capillary refill 4 seconds.
Flat. (Against tamponade and tension; he is empty.)
Circulation.mark: Neck veins flat: hypovolaemia, not tension or tamponade

Circulation.r: Soft, mildly tender right upper quadrant.

Circulation.t: Pelvis: look and gentle compression once
Circulation.r: No deformity, no pain on gentle pressure. You do not spring it again.
Springing the pelvis can dislodge clot. Look, and press gently once at most.

D E.r: GCS 14 (E3 V5 M6). Pupils equal and reactive. Glucose 7.2.

D E.t: Expose, then cover to keep warm
D E.r: No other injuries on the front. Warm blankets on. Temp 35.8.

steps.label: Talk to the nurse
steps.hint: Oxygen, two large-bore lines, bloods including crossmatch, and blood through the warmer.

opts.t: High-flow oxygen 15 L via non-rebreather
opts.mark: High-flow oxygen

opts.t: Two large-bore cannulae (14–16 G) in the antecubital fossae
opts.mark: Two large-bore IV lines

opts.t: Bloods: crossmatch 6 units, FBC, clotting with fibrinogen, U&E, lactate, venous gas
opts.mark: Sends crossmatch, clotting, gas and lactate
opts.r: Nurse Lam: Sent, crossmatch flagged urgent. Gas: pH 7.24, lactate 5.1, Hb 102.

opts.t: Start the O-negative blood now, then 1:1:1 red cells, plasma, platelets through the warmer
opts.mark: Transfuses blood early in a balanced ratio
opts.r: Nurse Lam: First unit running through the warmer. Plasma thawing.

opts.t: Aim for a systolic of about 80–90 until the bleeding is controlled
opts.mark: Permissive hypotension until haemorrhage control
opts.r: Nurse Lam: Titrating to a systolic of 80 to 90.

opts.t: Keep pushing saline until the pressure is normal
opts.r: Chasing a normal pressure with crystalloid dilutes clotting and raises the bleeding pressure.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Tranexamic acid inside 3 hours, and titrated analgesia.

opts.t: Tranexamic acid 1 g IV over 10 minutes, then 1 g over 8 hours
opts.mark: Tranexamic acid 1 g within 3 hours of injury

opts.t: Fentanyl 25–50 microgram IV, titrated
opts.mark: Titrated IV analgesia

opts.t: Calcium chloride 10% 10 mL with the blood
opts.mark: Replaces calcium during massive transfusion

opts.t: Adrenaline 1 mg IV
opts.r: He is not in arrest. Vasopressors in bleeding shock worsen outcome.

opts.t: Ketamine 2 mg/kg and suxamethonium to intubate now
opts.r: He is talking and oxygenating. Induction in this degree of shock can cause arrest; fix the chest and the volume first.

steps.label: Bedside tests
steps.hint: eFAST and a supine chest film in the bay. Not CT while he is unstable.

Bedside.r: Anechoic fluid above the right hemidiaphragm. Lung sliding present on both sides. Morison's pouch dry. No pericardial fluid.
Bedside.mark: eFAST: right haemothorax, abdomen and pericardium clear

Bedside.t: Supine chest X-ray in the bay
Bedside.r: Diffuse haze over the whole right hemithorax with vessels still visible. Trachea central.

Scanner.t: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis now
Scanner.r: He is not responding to resuscitation. CT is the 'doughnut of death' for an unstable patient.

steps.label: Right chest drain
steps.hint: Safe triangle, blunt dissection over the rib, finger sweep, large-bore tube, underwater seal, secure, film.

opts.t: Arm up behind the head; confirm the side on the patient and the film
opts.mark: Positions the arm up and confirms the side

opts.t: Mark the safe triangle: 5th intercostal space, just anterior to the mid-axillary line
opts.mark: Identifies the safe triangle

opts.t: Clean, drape, infiltrate lidocaine down to the pleura
opts.mark: Asepsis and local anaesthetic to the pleura

opts.t: 3 cm incision along the upper border of the 6th rib
opts.mark: Incises over the rib below the space

opts.t: Blunt dissection with forceps over the top of the rib into the pleura
opts.mark: Blunt dissection over the top of the rib

opts.t: Finger sweep inside the pleura
opts.mark: Finger sweep to exclude adhesions and organs

opts.t: Pass a large-bore tube (28–32 Fr) on a clamp, aimed posteriorly and up
opts.mark: Large-bore tube for haemothorax, no trocar

opts.t: Connect to an underwater seal; watch it swing and drain
opts.mark: Connects to underwater seal and checks swing
opts.r: 1600 mL of blood drains at once. It swings.

opts.t: Suture and dress the drain; repeat chest X-ray
opts.mark: Secures the drain and repeats the film

opts.t: Push the tube in on its sharp trocar
opts.r: The trocar can puncture the lung, heart, liver or great vessels. Never use it.

opts.t: Cut along the lower border of the rib
opts.r: The intercostal vessels and nerve run under the lower border. Go over the top of the rib below.

steps.label: Phone
steps.hint: 1600 mL at once is a massive haemothorax: call cardiothoracics for theatre.

opts.t: Cardiothoracic surgeon: 1600 mL on insertion, still shocked — thoracotomy
opts.mark: Recognises the thoracotomy threshold and calls cardiothoracics
opts.r: CTS registrar: Coming now. Theatre 2 is being opened.

opts.t: Theatre and anaesthetics: emergency thoracotomy, massive transfusion running
opts.mark: Alerts theatre and anaesthetics

opts.t: Clamp the drain to stop the bleeding
opts.r: Clamping hides the bleeding and can cause tension. Leave it open and measure the output.

opts.t: Admit to the surgical ward and repeat the film in the morning
opts.r: He has lost a third of his blood volume into his chest. He needs theatre.

steps.ask: The cardiothoracic registrar is here. Please hand over.
steps.label: Handover
steps.hint: Structured handover to the surgeon: situation, xABCDE findings, what you did, what he needs.

opts.t: ATMIST: 34, 40 minutes ago, handlebar to right chest, right massive haemothorax, 1600 mL drained, shocked on 2 units and TXA, needs thoracotomy
opts.mark: Structured handover with times, findings, treatment and plan
opts.r: You hand over in order. The surgeon repeats it back and takes him to theatre.

opts.t: He's got a chest injury, over to you
opts.r: No times, no volumes, no treatment given. The next team starts from zero.

qs.a: Over 1500 mL at once, or a third of blood volume
wrong: More than 500 mL at insertion, or any rib fracture
Any haemothorax seen on the supine chest X-ray
Any blood seen on eFAST, whatever the volume

qs.q: Which drain output means thoracotomy even after a smaller first drainage?
Why is this not a tension pneumothorax?
qs.a: Dull to percussion, trachea central, neck veins flat
qs.why: Tension is hyper-resonant with distended neck veins (unless hypovolaemic) and a trachea deviated away late.
wrong: He is still able to talk in sentences

qs.a: Latissimus dorsi, pectoralis major, 5th intercostal space
wrong: Sternum, nipple line and costal margin

qs.q: Tranexamic acid: dose and time limit?
qs.a: 1 g over 10 min, 1 g over 8 h, within 3 h
qs.why: CRASH-2: benefit falls with delay and giving it after 3 hours was associated with harm.
wrong: 1 g over 10 min, 1 g over 8 h, within 12 h
2 g bolus at any time after injury

rules.fail: You drained the chest before starting blood. Releasing 1.5 L of tamponading blood into an empty patient can precipitate arrest; have blood running first.
rules.ok: Blood was running before the drain went in.

rules.fail: Investigations came before the primary survey. Examine first; the eFAST and film are adjuncts to it.

badge.name: Pleural Plumber
badge.flavor: Dull, not hyper-resonant. Blood first, then the drain.

cards.q: Massive haemothorax is defined as an initial drain output of more than…
cards.why: Over 1500 mL immediately (or a third of blood volume) usually needs thoracotomy.

cards.q: Ongoing drain output that indicates thoracotomy?
cards.why: A persistent 200 mL/h means continuing bleeding that a drain will not stop.

cards.q: Percussion note over a massive haemothorax?
cards.why: Fluid is dull; air (pneumothorax) is hyper-resonant.

cards.q: Where do the intercostal vessels run?
options: Along the lower border of each rib
Along the upper border of each rib
cards.why: So you go over the top of the rib below the space.

cards.q: Tranexamic acid in trauma must start within…
cards.why: CRASH-2: late tranexamic acid was associated with harm.

cards.q: Preferred resuscitation fluid for a bleeding, shocked trauma patient?
options: Blood products in a balanced ratio
cards.why: Crystalloid is limited; early blood (1:1:1) reduces coagulopathy.

cards.q: Flat neck veins in a shocked chest-injured patient point to…
cards.why: Tension and tamponade raise venous pressure unless the patient is also empty.
